title: OmniPay POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization for a payments customer (OmniPay). Discussed average/peak QPS, concurrency, token size distributions, latency SLOs, cost targets, and security requirements. Redwood AE/SE to share pricing, run a small benchmark on Dedicated and hosted variants, and schedule a 1-week pilot to validate throughput/latency under representative traffic.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started in a sec. This is Sophie from Redwood, AE, and Ravi our SE is with me. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena Morris: hi lena here.
[00:08] Carlos Ruiz: carlos here.
[00:10] Aisha Khan: aisha - security.
[00:12] Tom Evans: tom product.
[00:14] Sophie Chen: awesome, thanks. Goal for today is to scope the POC around workload modeling - qps, concurrency and token distributions so we can give a reasonable benchmark plan and cost estimate. Ravi, want to kick off?
[00:25] Ravi Patel: yeah sure. so first, can you describe current traffic patterns and what you're trying to validate in the POC. like avg qps, peak qps, types of prompts, any tail events?
[00:36] Lena Morris: sure. high level, omniPay runs a few buyer-facing features: fraud detection assist (summary/scoring), automated replies for merchant support, and some embedding usage for search/rerank. Average across weekdays is around 20 qps, peak of maybe 120 to 160 qps during heavy morning/eod windows. bursty, depending on batch invoice runs.
[00:56] Tom Evans: for product, the critical use is the merchant support chat - short prompts 1-2 sentences and variable outputs, and then the fraud summary is longer, usually 40-300 tokens output.
[01:08] Carlos Ruiz: infra note - we run in GCP us-central, most traffic from NA, some EU. We need to keep data in our VPC for the pilot; so private or VPC peering is needed.
[01:18] Aisha Khan: security here - SOC2 in progress, and we require KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and RBAC. We'll need encryption at rest and in transit, and we need retention controls.
[01:28] Ravi Patel: great. those are common asks. for the workload model, can you share token distributions? even ballparks help.
[01:35] Lena Morris: yes, ballpark: input tokens are usually short - mean around 45 tokens, median 30, 90th percentile maybe 120, but some check runs send 600 token contexts when they include logs. output tokens: mean about 80, median 70, 95th percentile about 380 for long fraud summaries.
[01:50] Sophie Chen: okay that'll drive cost and latency. what are your latency SLOs? e.g., 95th or 99th P95.
[01:58] Tom Evans: Ideally sub 250ms p95 for short chat prompts. For the long fraud summaries we can tolerate 800-1000ms p95 but prefer under 600ms.
[02:08] Ravi Patel: makes sense. do you have concurrency targets? QPS alone doesn't capture burstiness.
[02:13] Carlos Ruiz: realistically concurrency of 40-60 during peaks, but ephemeral spikes to 120 for <5 mins during batch processing.
[02:20] Ravi Patel: good to know. so for modeling we'll use avg 20 qps sustained, peak sustained 150 qps, concurrency target 60 typical, spikes 120. We'll size for steady-state peak and ensure autoscale keeps up for spikes.
[02:33] Lena Morris: what's the usual approach from Redwood: hosted vs dedicated for this footprint?
[02:37] Sophie Chen: we usually recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation when customers have consistent sustained peaks like yours. Hosted can work for start, but for performance SLOs and VPC/networking Dedicated or Private is easier to guarantee. For the POC we can run a dedicated-like benchmark in hosted using reserved capacity, or we can deploy Redwood Dedicated in your VPC for a short pilot.
[02:54] Ravi Patel: technical detail - we need to know model family you're testing. do you have a preferred open model or LLM?
[03:00] Lena Morris: we've been experimenting with Mistral-style and Llama2 derivates, but for safety and auditability we'd prefer an open model variant. cost is a factor - quantized 4-bit would be ideal if quality holds.
[03:12] Ravi Patel: understood. we'll include quantized model profiles in the proposal. for benchmarking, we'll run 3 profiles: small-dialog (short prompts), long-summary (fraud), and embedding/rerank. Each profile will have a token distribution: small-dialog inputs mean 25 tokens, outputs 60, target p95 <250ms; long-summary inputs 120 mean, outputs 300 mean, target p95 <600ms; embeddings are batched - 256 dims, batch size varying.
[03:39] Tom Evans: curious about cost. what's ballpark per 1M tokens with quantized models on Dedicated vs hosted?
[03:45] Sophie Chen: we'll put exact pricing in the followup but rough order: hosted API for quantized open model could be 10-30 USD per 1M tokens depending on model and sequence length; Dedicated amortizes differently - you'd buy reserved capacity, so the per-token can be lower if you have steady usage. we'll give a SKU-level breakdown.
[04:03] Carlos Ruiz: network egress and VPC peering cost?
[04:06] Sophie Chen: we account for network egress separately; in a private deployment we can avoid public egress. for VPC peering there's setup but no per-request egress inside your cloud, though cross-region traffic carries cloud provider costs.
[04:18] Aisha Khan: on security - can you confirm KMS/HSM integration and audit logging? also where are logs stored?
[04:24] Ravi Patel: yes, we support KMS for key management and can push audit logs to your storage (e.g., BigQuery or S3) or to an endpoint; logs retention can be configured per your policy. we'll share the SOC2 artifact and architecture diagram.
[04:36] Lena Morris: nice. what does the POC look like timeline-wise?
[04:40] Sophie Chen: typical POC is 2-4 weeks: week 0 discovery/config, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 tuning and regression tests, optional week 3 durability and canary rollout. given your needs I'd recommend a 3-week pilot starting with shadow traffic (mirrored) then small % production ramp.
[04:55] Tom Evans: when can we start?
[04:56] Sophie Chen: we can start infra setup as soon as you sign the pilot SOW and provide network info. I'd propose kickoff 2026-04-05 to give 3 weeks for set up and scheduling.
[05:06] Carlos Ruiz: we'll need an IP allowlist or VPC peering details.
[05:09] Sophie Chen: yep we'll share network checklist.
[05:11] Ravi Patel: for benchmarks, we'll validate: throughput (qps), p95 latency, tail p99, per-token cost, and correctness/regression on a prompt set. can you produce a representative prompt set or allow us to use redacted examples?
[05:23] Lena Morris: we can provide a sanitized set of 500 prompts covering short chats and long fraud cases.
[05:29] Ravi Patel: perfect. we'll run the following tests: 1) single-request latency distribution with var token sizes; 2) sustained qps at 20qps for 1 hour; 3) peak soak at 150qps for 10 minutes; 4) concurrency spike test to 120 for 5 minutes. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rates, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:48] Tom Evans: sounds thorough. will you run tests on quantized variants too?
[05:51] Ravi Patel: yes - we'll run unquantized baseline and 4-bit quantized (or int8 if supported) and compare latency and quality on a small eval set.
[05:58] Aisha Khan: one more: data residency for EU customers - we may have to limit EU data. can the pilot be scoped to NA only?
[06:04] Sophie Chen: yes, we can restrict regions. we'll document multi-region routing and fallbacks.
[06:08] Lena Morris: okay next steps?
[06:10] Sophie Chen: recap: we'll share pricing and pilot SOW, security artifacts (SOC2, KMS integration doc), a network checklist, and a benchmark plan. Your team will share sanitized prompt set and confirm kickoff date. we'll also propose a dedicated capacity configuration for your peak targets.
[06:26] Tom Evans: who owns which items?
[06:28] Sophie Chen: I'll own pricing and SOW, Ravi will own benchmark plan and run tests, Lena/Carlos will share prompt set and network details, Aisha will confirm security checklist acceptance.
[06:38] Carlos Ruiz: ok we'll try to get the prompts and network stuff by 2026-03-18.
[06:43] Sophie Chen: perfect, we'll aim to have the pilot doc ready by 2026-03-18 as well and target kickoff 2026-04-05. thanks everyone we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[06:55] Lena Morris: thanks all.
[06:57] Sophie Chen: bye.
